name: Just
summary: A command runner that parses a justfile into recipes, resolves recipe dependencies and parameters, then invokes recipe bodies through a configured shell or script interpreter.

features.name: Recipe dependency graph
features.description: The official manual documents recipes that depend on other recipes, with dependencies executed before the dependent recipe and duplicate recipe invocations deduplicated within an invocation according to the documented argument rules.
benefits: Makes reusable setup and build ordering explicit in a small project file
Allows a named recipe to compose lower-level commands
costs: Dependency ordering and argument propagation must be reasoned about separately from shell commands
Recipe graphs do not by themselves provide artifact freshness or content-addressed rebuilds

features.name: Recipe parameter binding
features.description: Just documents positional, default, variadic, option, and exported recipe parameters, and its pinned analyzer validates parameter declarations and their use in recipe resolution.
benefits: Turns common command variations into explicit recipe interfaces
Supports forwarding arguments to dependencies and shell environments
costs: Parameter defaults, variadic forms, and dependency binding add invocation cases
Shell quoting and argument interpretation remain relevant at execution time

features.name: Configured shell execution
features.description: The official manual defines shell recipes whose lines are interpreted by a configured shell, supports alternate interpreters and shebang recipes, and documents environment-variable export settings.
benefits: Provides a portable recipe declaration while retaining shell-specific power
Allows projects to choose shell and environment propagation policy
costs: Results depend on the selected shell, host environment, and external commands
Shell recipes are orchestration declarations rather than hermetic action descriptions

mathematical_views.question: When does a set of parameterized recipes admit an invocation order with all dependency arguments bound?
assumptions: Recipes are vertices and dependency declarations are directed edges
An invocation carries bindings that must satisfy each recipe's parameter contract
The view abstracts shell process failures, filesystem effects, and recursive just invocations

mathematical_views.question: Which recipe declarations map to executable shell processes under a selected interpreter and environment?
assumptions: A recipe body is modeled as a command sequence interpreted by the configured shell
Environment exports and interpolated values are treated as process inputs
The view does not claim reproducibility or isolation from the host system

benefits: Readable named orchestration and explicit prerequisite ordering
costs: Graph execution does not automatically track file-derived freshness

benefits: Reusable recipes expose structured command variation
costs: Binding and quoting rules increase interface surface

benefits: Projects can use familiar shell and scripting ecosystems
costs: Host shell and environment behavior limit hermeticity and portability
